apps.localizedDescription: A fast, controller-friendly launcher that runs Windows games on iOS and iPadOS with Steam and GOG built in, powered by Wine, FEX and Metal via DXMT.

versions.localizedDescription:
**BCD is in alpha:** an early stage of development, before beta. Many games run, many do not yet, and things can break between builds. When a game fails, please send a log.

> **Everything new in this release is experimental and has been tried on only a few devices so far.** It may work great on yours, or it may not work at all. Either way, a log helps a lot.

> **Tried a game on an earlier build? Reset its settings first.** On the game's page: **Options › Recommended settings › Reset to Recommended**. The recommended list changed for 78 games in this release.

This build brings everything since 0.1.686: X-Plane 12 getting further, frame generation and an FPS counter for Vulkan games, Valve's November 2026 Steam client for BCD Dock, an experimental Steam for Windows, new pages in Settings, a round of fixes from the logs you sent, and a fix for Epic games on an external drive.

## X-Plane 12 (experimental)

X-Plane 12 gets further than before. On one iPhone it loaded, drew its cockpit and flew for six minutes. It is slow, it has been tried on that one iPhone only, and it is still experimental.

- **What you need:** iOS 26 or later and a device with a Metal 4 GPU. Start the game from your Steam library through BCD Dock, the way it was tried. On the game's page choose **Options › Recommended settings › Reset to Recommended**. The recommended settings carry everything below.
- **Lowest graphics settings (new):** the recommended settings now carry `xplane-graphics = lowest`.
  - **Why:** X-Plane saves its preferences only when it quits cleanly, and it never had. So every start took X-Plane's default settings and went straight into its first-time flight, with no main menu to lower them in. At those defaults the game stopped twice with "X-Plane is totally out of memory" and "Failed to allocate a GPU buffer", each time with BCD's address space full.
  - **What it does:** before X-Plane starts, BCD sets the default of each of its 14 graphics settings, in X-Plane's own `Resources/settings.txt`, to the lowest value. X-Plane's safe mode and every other byte of the file stay as they were. What you save in X-Plane still wins over these defaults.
  - **Going back:** X-Plane's own file is kept as `settings.txt.bcd-original` and put back when the line is removed.
- **A 4 GB swap file (new):** the recommended settings now carry `swap-mb = 4096`, `swap-mode = 2` and `swap-min-mb = 1`. BCD then moves game data to a file on the device's storage when memory runs short. Without it iOS ended the app at its 8 GB limit while the flight loaded (5 GB at the menu, 8.1 GB three minutes later). With it the flight ran for six minutes at a peak of 6.8 GB, and X-Plane quit cleanly from its own menu.
- **A freeze while loading:** one log showed the game compiling about 700 shader libraries over eight minutes. Then one more compile, a Metal library with no shader source, was still running 96 seconds later, and the game never drew again. BCD now refuses such a request at once instead of sending it to Metal's compiler. This was checked on a Mac. On the iPhone the next run took every shader from the cache, so the refusal itself has not been seen working there yet.
- **FPS counter:** it never worked for X-Plane, because Vulkan games did not reach it. It does now (see below).
- **What to expect:** about 13 to 18 FPS in flight at the lowest settings. The first start compiles shaders for several minutes (about 700 compiles over eight minutes in one log); later starts read them from the cache.
- **With frame generation** (below) X-Plane reached about 35 FPS shown in flight on that iPhone, from about 15 of its own (the HUD's `15+15`). iPads and other iPhones have not been tried. If it fails on yours, please send a log.

## Frame generation and the FPS counter for Vulkan games (experimental)

Vulkan games now get a working FPS counter and the frame-rate limit, on MoltenVK and on KosmicKrisp. Vulkan games that run on KosmicKrisp (the game's **Vulkan (experimental)** choice set to **KosmicKrisp**, which needs iOS 26 and a Metal 4 GPU) also get frame generation. X-Plane 12 on one iPhone is the only game and device all of this has run on so far: with frame generation it showed about 35 FPS in flight.

- **Apple frame interpolation:** on the game's page, **Display › Apple frame interpolation**: one frame between two, or up to three. iOS's own video frame interpolation makes the extra pictures from two of the game's frames. It needs no help from the game. It needs iOS 26, and it works only on KosmicKrisp, not on MoltenVK.
- **Lossless Scaling frame generation:** on the game's page, **Display › Lossless Scaling frame generation**: 2×, 3× or 4×.
  - **Lossless Scaling is not part of BCD.** It is a program sold on Steam. You need your own copy: sign in to Steam in BCD, then **Settings › Graphics › Lossless Scaling › Check my purchase and download from Steam**, once. BCD asks Steam whether your account owns it, downloads it with your account, and keeps its file sealed on this device. The purchase is checked again every week.
  - **For a Vulkan game,** BCD translates Lossless Scaling's frame generation shaders to Metal on the device when the game starts, from your own copy. The passes are then built in the background, which takes about 2 to 3 seconds. The translated file is removed when the session ends.
  - With Lossless Scaling on, Apple frame interpolation stays off for that game: one generator at a time.
- **Generated frames add a little delay.** They help most when the GPU has room to spare.
- **The frame-rate limit now holds Vulkan games,** on MoltenVK and on KosmicKrisp, as it always held DirectX games. Before, a Vulkan game ran at the screen's own rate whatever the limit said: X-Plane's menu ran at 120 FPS with the limit at 60. **This changes every Vulkan game:** one that ran above its limit now runs at it. `env.MADEIRA_VK_FPS_CAP = 0` in a game's settings turns it off. For Vulkan games the limit holds the game's own frames, and the generated frames come on top.
- **The FPS counter and the session summary now cover Vulkan games.** Before, every Vulkan game showed 0 FPS.
- **The in-game HUD shows the frames frame generation made,** after the game's own rate: `15+15 FPS` is 15 frames of the game's and 15 that frame generation made.
  - It counts Apple frame interpolation, Lossless Scaling and MetalFX frame generation, in DirectX games (through DXMT and BCD's Direct3D 12 bridge) and in Vulkan games on KosmicKrisp.
  - The frame time, the lows and the graph stay the game's own. The colour judges every frame shown against the limit.
  - Before, Lossless Scaling's frames in a Direct3D 11 game were counted as the game's own, so the rate was the sum of both.
  - On a device, this was seen only in X-Plane 12 (Vulkan). The DirectX paths were checked by tests, not yet on a device.
- **Not done:** Apple frame interpolation for Vulkan games on MoltenVK.

## The November 2026 Steam client in BCD Dock, and why you don't need Steam for Windows to play (experimental)

### What BCD Dock is
- BCD Dock starts your Steam games through **Valve's own Steam client library** (`steamclient64.dll`, the file the full Steam app for Windows also uses). It runs inside BCD without Steam's window, its web browser (Chromium) and its library.
- BCD Dock signs in with your own Steam sign-in. Valve's client then does what a game needs from Steam, as it does on a PC:
  - the online sign-in and the check that you own the game;
  - the game's Steam calls and any Steam DRM the game carries;
  - the per-account programs some games need (BCD Dock asks the client to prepare them before the start);
  - signing in offline;
  - Friends in games, when you turn them on in **Settings › Accounts › Steam**.
- BCD Dock is not a Steam emulator and bypasses nothing. Without Valve's sign-in and licence answer, a game does not start.

### What the November 2026 client adds
- **Settings › BCD Dock › Steam client** now offers three builds of Valve's client:
  - **Jan 2026**, the default, unchanged;
  - **Sep 2026**, unchanged: for games that ask for a newer Steam interface than January's has, such as Grim Dawn, Hades II and Enshrouded. No Friends;
  - **Nov 2026**, new: the client Valve published on 13 November 2026.
- **Newer Steam interfaces.** Nov 2026 has five interfaces that the January client lacks: `SteamUser024`, `SteamInput007`, `SteamNetworkingSockets013`, `SteamGameServer016` and `SteamMatchMakingServers003`. A game built with a newer Steam library can stop at its start with "Missing interface adapter", with "No SteamUtils011" or with a "Steam is not running" box. Nov 2026 has the newer interfaces such a game asks for. A game may still ask for something newer than Valve's client of 13 November has.
- **Friends** work with Nov 2026, as with Jan 2026. Sep 2026 has none.
- **BCD's suggestions** now name Nov 2026 when a game stops because its Steam library is newer than the client (for `SteamUtils011`, Sep 2026 has the interface too).
- **Switching** moves your installed games, saves and settings to the chosen client, and you can switch back at any time. The old client's folder is renamed and kept. Nothing is deleted.
- **A build BCD Dock does not know is refused before sign-in** with report code 30, not guessed at. BCD Dock checks the exact client file and the exact calls it makes into it, build by build. Valve moved four of the client's internal calls (the two ownership questions and the two offline sign-in calls) by one slot in this build, so each build now has its own table.
- **Tried so far,** on one iPhone: the switch to Nov 2026 and back; games started through BCD Dock; a game whose per-account program Steam prepares; an offline start; Friends; a game that stopped on a missing Steam interface. The table for this build was made by reading Valve's file, without a device. These runs are its first tests.
- **January 2026 stays the default.** Nov 2026 is less tested. Choose it when a game needs it. If a game no longer starts with it, switch back.

### Why you don't need Steam for Windows to play
- **The game already talks to Valve's real client.** Sign-in, ownership, Steam's calls, per-account programs, offline play and Friends all go through the same client library that BCD Dock runs. The full Steam app adds a window around that library. A game does not need the window.
- **Memory.** Steam's window is a web browser. On the one iPhone tried it held 2.3 to 3.4 GB of the 8 GB iOS gives BCD, much of BCD's address space and a JIT pool of up to 1.1 GB for its own code. Heavy games need all of that for themselves. Through BCD Dock they get it.
- **Each game's own BCD settings.** Through BCD Dock every game starts with its recommended settings and the ones you set on its page. A game started from Steam for Windows runs inside Steam's session, with that session's settings. X-Plane 12, started that way, found no Vulkan driver and quit after nine seconds.
- **BCD's own library covers the rest:** downloads and updates, DLC you own, beta versions, Workshop items, Steam Cloud saves and Launch options.

### When Steam for Windows can still help
These are things BCD itself does not do:
- buying games or DLC in the Steam store;
- Steam's own settings and account pages, and Steam's community pages;
- your friends list and chat outside a game (BCD offers Friends in a game);
- your achievements: BCD does not show them;
- updating a game that Valve's client installed in its own library folder. BCD lists and starts such a game but does not update it.

Steam's app on your phone, or Steam's website, can do most of these too.

## Steam for Windows (experimental, off unless you turn it on): not for playing games

> **Steam for Windows is not a way to play your games.** Play them through BCD Dock, as before. Turn this on only if you want to look around in Valve's own Steam app.

- **What it is:** Valve's full Steam client for Windows, with its own window, store and library, in a Windows desktop inside BCD. Turn it on in **Settings › BCD Dock › Steam for Windows**, then install it there. BCD gets it from Valve's own servers and checks every file. You sign in in Steam's own window; BCD hands it no sign-in.
- **What it is for:** the store, your library, Friends, the Workshop and Steam's own settings.
- **Why not for games:** a game started from it runs inside Steam's own session. It does not get the settings BCD gives that game, and Steam's window uses much of the memory a game needs. Heavy games do not fit beside it. In tests on one iPhone it opened, signed in and showed the library, but the games tried from it did not run.
- **It needs a lot of memory:** it is made for devices with a large address space and a memory limit of 6 GB or more, such as an 8 GB iPhone signed with the larger memory limit, or an M-series iPad. An update from Valve can break it.
- **Games and DLC are shared both ways** (**Share games with BCD Dock**, on by default; it takes effect at the next start):
  - **BCD Dock's games show as installed in Steam for Windows,** from the same files: one copy of each game, used by both. Steam may update or check them there. BCD keeps a one-time safety copy of BCD Dock's library records. This part was seen working on one iPhone.
  - **A game you install in Steam for Windows shows in BCD's library** and starts through BCD Dock. BCD neither updates it nor changes its DLC.
  - **Steam keeps BCD Dock's DLC choices.** Valve's client installs every DLC your account owns by itself, such as X-Plane 12's free scenery packs, while BCD installs only the DLC you chose. Before each session BCD tells Steam to leave off the DLC you did not choose. If BCD cannot look a game's DLC up (offline, or not signed in), Steam may still download them. At the end of the session, what you ticked, installed, unticked or removed in Steam goes into BCD's DLC choice.
  - **Not yet tried on a device:** the DLC choices and the other direction of the sharing.
- After a Steam for Windows session, restart BCD before you start a game through BCD Dock.

## New in Settings

None of these has been tried on a device yet.

- **Settings › Recommended settings (new page):** every game BCD has recommended settings for, in the list in use. Search by game name, program or Steam App ID, and filter by Steam, Epic, GOG or DRM-free. A game's page shows how it is matched, its switches, every line with whether your build has it, the lines only a device with less than 10 GB of RAM gets, and its notes. It only reads; nothing is changed from there.
- **Settings › Memory & performance › In the background › CPU limit in the background:** 50% (the standard, unchanged), 65%, 80%, 100% or no limit. It sets how much of one core BCD uses while it keeps a game or a download going in the background. At 50% a big download is slow. iOS closes an app that averages above about 80% for a minute, so 100% and no limit can get BCD closed. It applies the next time you leave BCD.
- **Bug reports carry your last game's log by default** (**Settings › Feedback › Attach my last game's log**).
  - The row names the log: the game, the day and the size. Turn it off and BCD keeps that choice.
  - The log is cleaned on the device before it goes: user names, e-mail addresses, IP addresses and account IDs are taken out.
  - An idea or another message still carries a log only when you turn it on.
- **End the game now:** a game that ignores **Close** used to leave you only the way of closing BCD. After 45 seconds the session's top line says so, and the in-game menu offers **End the game now**. Unsaved progress is lost. Not offered on the Windows desktop or while a game is still starting. A new session also no longer counts a process that an earlier session left running.
- **Frame cap: 20 and 25 FPS** (**Settings › Graphics › Frame cap**, now 20, 24, 25, 30, 40 and 60). Frame generation doubles them to 40 and 50. The cap now also holds Vulkan games, which it did not before, and the HUD judges its colour against it.

## Programs built on Qt 6 (experimental)

Qt 6 programs need Windows' ICU libraries (`icuuc.dll` and `icuin.dll`), which Wine does not have. Such a program ended at once with a missing-library error (c0000135): Bloodborne's PC port launcher, Anki, the Albion launcher. BCD now carries ICU 78.3 (Unicode 17.0), trimmed to what Qt needs, and gives it to a program that asks for it. Bloodborne's launcher has the line in its recommended settings. Auto-tune adds it for another Qt 6 program that stops this way; an older build is told to update. ICU's licence is in the app's notices. Not yet tried on a device.

## Fixed in games (from the logs you sent)

Each was made from a log and checked by tests on a Mac. None has been tried on a device yet.

- **Half-Life 2** stopped within seconds of starting, every time. BCD took the game's first write next to a protected page of its own for a write to the protected page. With `env.MADEIRA_GUARD_NEIGHBOUR_PASS = 1`, in its recommended settings, such a write goes through.
- **The Binding of Isaac** crashed on a memory block that BCD placed outside the part of the address space a 32-bit game can reach. A 32-bit game's memory now stays inside its own part, or the request is refused (`env.MADEIRA_WOW_ALLOC_INSIDE = 1`, in its recommended settings).
- **S.T.A.L.K.E.R. Clear Sky and Call of Pripyat** stopped at a shader whose loop BCD's shader compiler cannot write for Shader Model 3. With `env.MADEIRA_HLSL_LOOP_FALLBACK = 40` the loop is written as up to 40 repeated steps. Their recommended settings carry it.
- **DOOM 3: BFG Edition** crashed in BCD's OpenGL when it asked about an empty sync object (`glIsSync(0)`). That now answers as OpenGL defines it, for every game on BCD's OpenGL.
- **METAL GEAR SOLID V** stopped at "Failed to load SteamAPI". It checks the signature of `steam_api64.dll`, and the chain ends in a root certificate BCD's web list lacks (VeriSign Class 3 Public Primary Certification Authority - G5). With `env.MADEIRA_CODESIGN_ROOTS = 1`, in its recommended settings, that one root, pinned by its SHA-256, counts for code signatures. Nothing is added to the root store, so web connections never use it.
- **Buckshot Roulette** needs `--rendering-driver opengl3` to find a graphics driver. BCD cut a program name at its first blank, so the line for "Buckshot Roulette.exe" never matched. Names with a blank now work in `env.MADEIRA_CHILD_ARGS`, and the game's recommended settings pass the argument.
- **A game that froze for good after a click on its window's frame** (title bar and edges of a windowed game) no longer does. The size and move loop of such a window now takes taps and keys. `env.MADEIRA_GAME_INPUT_WAKE = 0` turns it off.
- **EA games started through Steam** (Battlefield 4, Mass Effect: Andromeda, Need for Speed, STAR WARS Jedi: Fallen Order, The Sims 4, Unravel and others) go through EA's launcher, whose background service needs Windows' service manager. BCD Dock now starts Wine's service manager for a game whose install script runs EA's installer. These games, and FIFA 22 and Need for Speed: Most Wanted (2012), also get the Wine libraries the EA app asks for in their recommended settings.
- **A 64-bit game's big program or library that did not fit the room left in BCD's code memory** was copied anyway, the copy was refused, and the game never started (Cyberpunk 2077's XeSS libraries and others). Such a file now runs from its own file instead.
- **Cyberpunk 2077:** its recommended settings now keep its images out of the code memory and handle its 16, 64 and 32 GB address reservations, and also match its launcher program. Auto-tune has a rule for its overlapping reservations.
- **Spider-Man:** Marvel's Spider-Man Remastered and Miles Morales get the swap file from the first start on devices with less than 10 GB of RAM. Spider-Man 2 gets the per-process keyed event setting.
- **More:** Dark Souls: Remastered is told it has 8 GB, so its minimum-memory box does not stop it. NARUTO: Ultimate Ninja STORM and The Elder Scrolls IV: Oblivion get a DirectInput view of the controller. TEKKEN 7 and Little Nightmares get Wine's Windows Error Reporting library. eFootball PES 2021 gets Wine's DirectX diagnostics library. Detroit: Become Human gets Vulkan on KosmicKrisp. ULTIMATE MARVEL VS. CAPCOM 3 gets BCD's 64-bit Direct3D 9. FINAL FANTASY TACTICS gets new Direct3D 12 settings. Rows now also name a game's program, so a copy outside Steam gets them too (see the list below).

## Resident Evil 4 (2005) and other Direct3D 9 games: copying only what a draw reads (experimental)

A player's log showed Resident Evil 4 (2005) running at 60 FPS for 30 seconds and then at 4 to 6 FPS. The game locks its dynamic vertex buffers about 210 times a frame, 1 to 256 bytes each, and every draw after a lock copied the whole 3.8 MB buffer to the GPU: 788 MB a frame in the log. The GPU was 5 to 8% busy.

- **New, off unless set:** `env.DXMT_D9_VB_RANGE = 1`. A draw that is not indexed then copies only the vertex bytes it reads. Indexed and instanced draws, draws from the game's own memory and any stream whose layout is doubtful keep the whole copy. With the line off, nothing changes.
- **It is on, through their recommended settings (from build 710), for Resident Evil 4 (2005) and for every game whose logs showed the same copy** (10 MB or more a frame): Vampire: The Masquerade - Bloodlines, Alan Wake, Blur, Ultra Street Fighter IV, Mount & Blade: Warband, Team Fortress 2, Garry's Mod, Left 4 Dead 2, Counter-Strike: Source, Half-Life 2, Half-Life 2: Deathmatch, No More Room in Hell, Call of Duty: World at War, Call of Duty: Black Ops, Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 3, Grand Theft Auto IV, The Elder Scrolls V: Skyrim (2011), Splinter Cell: Double Agent and Burnout Paradise. Games that draw mostly with indexed draws (the Source engine games, for example) may gain little. The log says `[vb-range] madeira-bcd on`.
- **Not yet tried on a device.** If you play one of these games, please send a log.

## From pull requests

Thank you to the people who sent these.

- **Touch-control editor: select several controls at once.** Drag from an empty spot in the editor to select several buttons or sticks, then move them together, or resize them together with a pinch or the Size slider. Guides appear while you move a control near another one's edge or centre, and it snaps into line. (pull request #69)
- **Teardown: the missing half of the scene.** The game draws much of its world with Direct3D 12 indirect draws that carry several arguments per draw, and BCD skipped them. With `indirect-expand = 1` BCD now draws them from the game's own records. It is off by default, because a game that changes those records after recording would draw stale ones. Teardown's recommended settings turn it on. Tried on one device by the pull request's author. (pull request #67)
- **Auto-tune judges two kinds of sessions correctly** (pull request #64):
  - a line BCD writes about the previous run is no longer read as this session's, so a game that closed after a few seconds is no longer scored as if it had played for minutes;
  - Windows' shortcut helper (`winemenubuilder.exe`), which Wine tries to start and BCD does not ship, no longer makes a session that played look like a crash.
- **A rare crash when a thread ends** (pull request #64), behind a setting that is off by default (`env.MADEIRA_EXIT_POOL_SKIP = 1`). It now also clears the places where the system keeps the first objects of a thread's memory pool. BCD's own tests now pass on the build Mac.

## Auto-tune

27 rules are new and 14 changed. Each has a log it was made from.

- **Steam client stops** now point to **Nov 2026** (see above).
- **New fixes it can try:**
  - a game that checks the memory it is told and refuses to start gets 8 GB told;
  - a game started through EA's Steam launcher gets Windows' service manager;
  - a game that stops with "needs Vulkan" gets Vulkan on KosmicKrisp turned on;
  - a game's .NET runtime that reserved 256 GB of address space gets a 16 GB range;
  - a Java game that stopped right after its first garbage collection gets the simple collector or plain code memory (Project Zomboid, Slay the Spire);
  - an OpenGL game that stopped at a `ChoosePixelFormat` error or at SDL3's "OpenGL 3.2 is required" box gets BCD's own OpenGL driver turned on (Old School RuneScape, Underkeep);
  - a program built on Chromium whose 16 GB request found no room gets a smaller block (Slow Roads);
  - a 32-bit game that plays but spends most of its frame time on slow memory writes gets ordinary memory, kept only if it then plays without the slowdown.
- **Answers that say what to do:**
  - a game started as a program file that asks for Steam ("Steam is not running"): start it from your Steam library through BCD Dock;
  - an EA game that starts itself through EA's Origin launcher: start it with Steam instead;
  - a device where iOS gives BCD only 4 GB: too small for the game. Lower its own texture and shadow settings.
- **It can add a DLL to a game's own list of DLLs.** Until now a rule that wanted one more DLL was skipped when the recommended settings already had a list. It now adds its names after the list's, and never drops one.
- **More starts count as failures,** so a fix is offered after them: a BCD Dock game that showed an error box and drew no frame, a game that closed by itself before its first picture, and a start where the JIT pool was refused. A replay of 6,303 earlier logs changes 24 verdicts, each a failure that had been missed.
- **Several rules were narrowed** so they stop matching games they did not help (the Chromium address-space rule matched 325 earlier logs, and only 65 were the real case).

  - Fighting and sports: ULTIMATE MARVEL VS. CAPCOM 3, NARUTO: Ultimate Ninja STORM, eFootball PES 2021, Ultra Street Fighter IV.
  - With the Direct3D 9 vertex change only: Alan Wake, Blur, Mount & Blade: Warband, Team Fortress 2, Garry's Mod, Left 4 Dead 2, Half-Life 2: Deathmatch, Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 3 (2011), The Elder Scrolls V: Skyrim (2011), Splinter Cell: Double Agent.
  - Other: Teardown (from a pull request), VRChat, Don't Starve, Echo Weaver, Cryptid Park, Old School RuneScape, Slow Roads, Underkeep, We Steal From Old People: The Game, Fields of Mistria.
- **Updated:**
  - X-Plane 12 and Red Dead Redemption 2 (not Steam: its Launcher.exe beside RDR2.exe).
  - Big releases: Marvel's Spider-Man Remastered, Marvel's Spider-Man: Miles Morales, Marvel's Spider-Man 2, Cyberpunk 2077, Clair Obscur: Expedition 33, HITMAN World of Assassination, FINAL FANTASY TACTICS - The Ivalice Chronicles, METAL GEAR SOLID V: THE PHANTOM PAIN, DARK SOULS III, Dark Souls: Remastered, Rise of the Tomb Raider, TEKKEN 7, Dead Space (2023).
  - EA, Need for Speed and FIFA: Need for Speed: Most Wanted (2012), Need for Speed: Most Wanted (speed.exe), FIFA 22.
  - The Direct3D 9 vertex change also went into Vampire: The Masquerade - Bloodlines, Call of Duty: Black Ops, Grand Theft Auto IV, Counter-Strike: Source, Call of Duty: World at War, Half-Life 2, No More Room in Hell and Burnout Paradise.
  - Others: Unrailed! 2: Back on Track, Batman: Arkham City GOTY, Requiem: Avenging Angel, S.T.A.L.K.E.R. (X-Ray engine games), Saints Row: The Third, Sleeping Dogs: Definitive Edition, Call of Duty: Black Ops, The Binding of Isaac: Rebirth, Buckshot Roulette, The Elder Scrolls IV: Oblivion, THE KING OF FIGHTERS XIV, Day of the Tentacle Remastered.

## Fixed: Epic games on an external drive

- **Installs on some external drives were refused for space** although the drive had plenty of room. In one log the drive answered 0 free to the question BCD asked, and every Epic install was refused at once. BCD now reads the drive's free space the way its Steam downloads already do. A tester confirmed it.
- **On a drive BCD asks only for the room the game's files still lack.** exFAT has no sparse files, so a file created at its final size already holds its room.
- **A refused install writes the space it needed and the space it found into the log.**

## Known issues

- **X-Plane 12** is slow (about 13 to 18 FPS of its own in flight at the lowest settings, about 35 shown with frame generation) and has been tried on one iPhone only. Its first start compiles shaders for several minutes.
- **Apple frame interpolation** does not work for Vulkan games on MoltenVK yet.
- **Vulkan frame generation:** the frame-rate limit holds the game's own frames; the generated frames come on top of it.

Install help, game reports and ideas: the BCD-Games Discord is open, https://discord.gg/43TmupTVug
